Claude.notes: Rigorous, well-sourced taxonomy of AI-generated false content across deepfakes, LLM hallucinations, and synthetic propaganda. The Gutenberg-to-Descartes historical framing creates strong problem-setup for the technical distinctions that follow. Chat-based labs are executable and quiz questions genuinely test judgment (e.g., the adversarial arms-race framing) rather than recall. The softest point is delivery pacing on long lessons — Advanced learners can handle it, but explicit mid-lesson checkpoints would help.
Claude.topIssue: Story-to-concept flow could better invite learner discovery of the taxonomy rather than presenting it fully formed after the case study.

Gemini.notes: Technical claims about diffusion models, next-token prediction, and VALL-E's three-second voice-cloning threshold check out. Case attributions (Pentagon Midjourney artifacts, Turley/GPT hallucination, New Hampshire robocall) are accurate. Some category boundaries between hallucination and synthetic propaganda could be tightened for edge cases where an LLM is used deliberately to fabricate.
Gemini.topIssue: The definitional boundary between 'hallucination' (LLM confident fabrication) and 'synthetic propaganda' (deliberate LLM-produced falsehood) is asserted but not disambiguated for overlap cases.

Perplexity.notes: Case studies are two-to-three years old but structurally illustrative. The lesson explicitly dates itself with the phrase 'less than eighteen months' about model availability — that framing needs refreshing for a 2026 reader. Detection-tool discussion (GPTZero, C2PA) reflects a 2023-early-2024 snapshot; the 2025-26 provenance and watermarking landscape has moved.
Perplexity.topIssue: Detection tool claims (GPTZero, C2PA rollout status) reflect an early-2024 snapshot; a 2026 learner encounters a significantly changed provenance and watermarking landscape not represented here.

Claude.notes: Solid reverse-image toolkit walkthrough (Google Images, TinEye, Yandex, InVID/WeVerify). The SIFT protocol mapping to visual verification is clean and directly executable. Quiz on efficient workflow ordering genuinely tests procedural judgment. Boston Marathon Sunil Tripathi case anchors the lesson emotionally, though it's a decade-old example.
Claude.topIssue: Lesson opens with the Sunil Tripathi case as a recycled-image example, but that misidentification predates modern reverse-image tooling by years; a more recent case (2024 Gaza/Ukraine image recycling) would tighten currency.

Gemini.notes: Tool descriptions (TinEye 'oldest first' sort, Yandex's Cyrillic-language strength, InVID keyframe extraction) are technically correct. Geolocation methodology using shadow direction, architecture, and vegetation is properly framed. Boston Marathon and Australian bushfire cases are accurately attributed. Category boundaries between 'recycled' and 'manipulated' images could be sharper.
Gemini.topIssue: The lesson treats 'recycled images' (real photo, wrong context) and 'manipulated images' (cropped/composited) as taxonomically separate but does not clarify how a cropped-and-recycled image should be classified.

Perplexity.notes: Tools recommended remain the current standard for 2026 reverse-image verification (Google Images, TinEye, Yandex, InVID) with no critical gaps in the toolkit. Heavy reliance on Boston Marathon (2013) and Australian bushfire (2019-20) cases is the main currency concern — both are structurally sound but visibly aged.
Perplexity.topIssue: Boston Marathon (2013) and Australian bushfires (2019-20) are structurally correct but aged for a 2026 audience — a 2024 Middle East misinformation case would land harder.

Claude.notes: Crimea 2014 → RAND firehose model → Bannon 'flood the zone' → AI content farms is a clean narrative escalation that mirrors the actual historical arc. The 'adversarial generalization failure' framing for detection is correctly applied and gives learners a systemic lens. Labs prompt learners to reason from mechanism to consequence, which fits the level.
Claude.topIssue: The transition from the RAND 2016 firehose model to modern AI amplification could more explicitly walk learners through the connecting mechanism, rather than juxtaposing the two eras.

Gemini.notes: MIT Media Lab 2019 finding on false news spreading six times faster on Twitter, RAND Paul-Matthews 2016 firehose framing, NewsGuard 49-to-600 site growth, and the 2024 Alliance for Securing Democracy narrative-laundering report are all cited accurately. Technical mechanism claims about adversarial dynamics hold up.
Gemini.topIssue: Adversarial generalization is stated as the reason detection loses the arms race, but the underlying mechanism — that detector training signal is exploitable by generator training — is not made explicit.

Perplexity.notes: The 2024 European Parliament narrative-laundering ASD case is a strong currency anchor. The Bannon 2018 quote and RAND 2016 model still frame the tactics correctly and remain the canonical references. Additional 2025-26 material on state-linked LLM-driven info-ops would strengthen contemporary relevance further.
Perplexity.topIssue: The 2024 ASD case is the most current anchor; several supporting citations reach back to 2014-2019 and don't reflect 2025-26 developments in LLM-driven state info-ops.

Claude.notes: SIFT is the clearest procedural payload of the entire course, and this module lands it. Lateral reading vs. vertical reading is precisely distinguished with the Stanford 2022 study on professional fact-checkers as the anchor. Taiwan case study as 'democratic infrastructure' framing gives learners a systemic hook. Highest lab-executability of the four modules — SIFT is directly performable in 90 seconds.
Claude.topIssue: The Dominion Voting 2020 opening is a great problem-setup, but the '90 seconds to trace' framing is asserted rather than demonstrated in-flow; a walk-through screenshot sequence would make the payoff more visceral.

Gemini.notes: SIFT four-move framework is defined precisely. Stanford History Education Group 2019 study (96% source-check failure), Taiwan literacy program, and NewsGuard 2024 Israel-Palestine documentation are accurately cited. Strong technical grounding throughout. Caulfield's University of Washington affiliation is stated but worth a light fact-check pass.
Gemini.topIssue: The module cites Mike Caulfield as 'a digital literacy researcher at the University of Washington' — Caulfield's affiliation has shifted institutions over time and the current title deserves verification.

Perplexity.notes: The module's core protocol ages exceptionally well because SIFT is medium-independent. Taiwan case study is still contemporary. The one gap: nothing on provenance-side infrastructure (C2PA, watermarking, content credentials) that has become part of the 2025-26 verification stack alongside SIFT-style lateral reading.
Perplexity.topIssue: SIFT and lateral reading remain current best practice, but the module doesn't reference AI-native provenance tools (C2PA, watermarking, content credentials) that have emerged as complements in the last 18 months.
